newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SembCorp in S$200 mln utilities project.
newsitem.headline: SembCorp in S$200 mln utilities project.

text.p: Sembawang Utilities and Terminals Pte Ltd (SUT) said on Monday it has embarked on a Singapore $200 million expansion project for its utilities centre on Pulau Sakra in Singapore.
SUT is a joint venture between SembCorp Ltd's Sembawang Engineering and Construction Pte Ltd, Powersin S.A., JTC International Pte Ltd and EDB Investments Pte Ltd.
SUT is building a facility in Pulau Sakra to provide utilties storage and terminal services to chemical and petrochemical companies on a soon-to-be-merged group of seven islands off Singapore.
The merged islands, to be named Jurong Island, will become an integrated services petrochemical island.
The first phase of SUT's centre costs S$250 million, of which S$50 million had already been invested in April, 1996, a statement said.
SUT is going ahead with the S$200 million investment due to increasing demand for utilities by it clients, it said.
The completion of the S$200 million expansion is scheduled for late 1998 and will mark the start of full commercial operation for SUT on Pulau Sakra, it said.

The centre will initially provide steam, cooling water, chilled water among others to chemical plants on the island. It will also provide users with chemical storage, terminal facilities and waste water treatment services.
